cards.meaning: A period of two weeks.
cards.example: The school holidays lasted a fortnight.
cards.trap: Writing fourthnight because the word sounds as if it begins with fourth.

rule.text: Write fort before night.

cards.meaning: Drawn from a wide range of styles or sources.
cards.example: Bola chose an eclectic mix of songs for the Abuja concert.
cards.trap: Leaving out the second c.

rule.text: The middle is lect, with a c before the t.

cards.meaning: The way a word is spoken.
cards.example: The class practised the pronunciation of words before assembly.
cards.trap: Keeping the ou from pronounce.

rule.text: The noun uses nun in the middle.

cards.meaning: Giving extra help or support.
cards.example: The auxiliary nurse helped at the village clinic.
cards.trap: Writing double l or dropping the i after l.

rule.text: Write aux-il-iary, with one l.

cards.meaning: Most important or first in rank.
cards.example: Safety was the foremost concern on the trip to Kano.
cards.trap: Writing formost by dropping the first e.

rule.text: Join fore and most.

cards.meaning: Relating to medical care for animals.
cards.example: The farmer went to a veterinary clinic in Jos.
cards.trap: Dropping a syllable in the middle.

rule.text: Write veter before inary.

cards.meaning: Worked out the details of something complicated.
cards.example: The pupils unravelled the puzzle at the Abuja science fair.
cards.trap: Using the US single-l past form in a British spelling exercise.

rule.text: Double the final l before ed in British spelling.

cards.meaning: The use of words that imitate sounds.
cards.example: The teacher used buzz to explain onomatopoeia at our school.
cards.trap: Putting ie where the spelling has ei.

rule.text: End the word with poeia.

cards.note: The PDF text repeats onomatopoeia in two options. The card teaches the dictionary spelling only.

cards.meaning: Producing a bright glow, as in some lamps.
cards.example: A fluorescent tube lit the examination hall in Kano.
cards.trap: Swapping the u and o.

rule.text: Write fluor before escent.

cards.meaning: A disagreement or a set of reasons for a point of view.
cards.example: An argument broke out over the fare at the bus park.
cards.trap: Keeping the e from argue before ment.

rule.text: Drop the final e in argue before adding ment.

cards.meaning: Impossible to reverse or take back.
cards.example: The lawyer told Amina the agreement was irrevocable.
cards.trap: Dropping the second r.

rule.text: Join ir and revocable to get a double r.

cards.note: The PDF key indicates a different stressed syllable from Cambridge. The card teaches spelling only.

cards.meaning: Making someone feel physically at ease.
cards.example: The new seats in the Abuja bus were comfortable.
cards.trap: Leaving out the t heard weakly in speech.

rule.text: Keep the whole word comfort before able.

cards.meaning: Make someone unable to work or act normally.
cards.example: The doctor said a bad sprain could incapacitate a runner.
cards.trap: Using s where the word has its second c.

rule.text: Keep capac in the middle before itate.

cards.meaning: Words or actions that give someone confidence.
cards.example: The Kano pupils welcomed the coach's encouragement.
cards.trap: Dropping the e from encourage.

rule.text: Keep the final e of encourage before adding ment.

cards.meaning: A place to stay or live.
cards.example: The club found accommodation for the Abuja tournament.
cards.trap: Writing only one c or one m.

rule.text: Use both cc and mm.

cards.meaning: The details of where someone lives or works.
cards.example: Emeka wrote his address on the school form.
cards.trap: Writing only one d.

rule.text: Double the d and the final s.

cards.meaning: The first part or start of something.
cards.example: We sang at the beginning of assembly.
cards.trap: Writing one n before ing.

rule.text: Double the final n of begin before adding ing.

cards.meaning: Think something is true.
cards.example: I believe the market opens before eight.
cards.trap: Reversing the i and e.

rule.text: The last four letters are ieve.

cards.meaning: Work involving trade, or a company doing that work.
cards.example: Her catering business supplies a school in Kano.
cards.trap: Spelling it like its short first spoken syllable.

rule.text: Write busi, then ness.

cards.meaning: A group appointed to handle particular work.
cards.example: The school committee met before assembly.
cards.trap: Leaving out one t.

rule.text: Double the m, t and final e.

cards.meaning: The surroundings or conditions in which something lives.
cards.example: The Abuja club cleaned the environment around its school.
cards.trap: Dropping the n before ment.

rule.text: Keep both n's in environ before ment.

cards.meaning: A chance to do something.
cards.example: The school fair gave Ada an opportunity to sell her baskets.
cards.trap: Writing only one p.

rule.text: Double the p after the opening o.

cards.meaning: Get something given or sent to you.
cards.example: The pupils will receive their books at assembly.
cards.trap: Putting i before e in the ending.

rule.text: Write e before i after c in receive.

cards.meaning: Suggest that someone choose or do something.
cards.example: The librarian will recommend a book for the class.
cards.trap: Using one m or two c's.

rule.text: Use one c and two m's.

cards.meaning: A place where people pay for a prepared meal.
cards.example: We stopped at a restaurant in Ibadan after the match.
cards.trap: Dropping the u after a.

rule.text: Write restau before rant.

cards.meaning: A public message that promotes something.
cards.example: Bisi saw an advertisement for the used bicycle in Aba.
cards.trap: Dropping the e in the ending.

rule.text: Keep the e in advertise before adding ment.

cards.meaning: Introduces a fact that contrasts with the rest of a sentence.
cards.example: Although it rained, the Kano team played the match.
cards.trap: Giving it two l's or a final t.

rule.text: Write al plus though.

cards.meaning: At all times or on every occasion.
cards.example: The bus driver always greets the pupils at the gate.
cards.trap: Adding a second l at the start.

rule.text: Write al plus ways, with one l.

cards.meaning: Feel grateful for something or recognise its value.
cards.example: The teachers appreciate the help from the PTA.
cards.trap: Dropping one p.

rule.text: Begin with app, using two p's.

cards.meaning: Ready to be used or obtained.
cards.example: Three seats were available on the bus to Enugu.
cards.trap: Putting the i before the l.

rule.text: Write avail before able.

cards.meaning: Very pleasing in appearance or sound.
cards.example: The class admired a beautiful mural in Abuja.
cards.trap: Writing double l or shortening the vowel group.

rule.text: Keep eau near the start and use one final l.

cards.meaning: Gives the reason something happened.
cards.example: Our assembly moved indoors because rain was coming.
cards.trap: Writing ou in the second half of the word.

rule.text: Write be followed by cause.

cards.meaning: A vehicle with two wheels that you move by pedalling.
cards.example: Musa rode his bicycle to the village market.
cards.trap: Replacing the y with i.

rule.text: Keep cycle after bi.

cards.meaning: Someone you work with.
cards.example: My aunt and her colleague teach at a school in Jos.
cards.trap: Dropping the a from league.

rule.text: Write col plus league.

cards.meaning: Easy to fit into one's plans or needs.
cards.example: The new bus stop is convenient for pupils in Yaba.
cards.trap: Putting an i before the n in the middle.

rule.text: Write ven in the middle of convenient.

cards.meaning: Someone who buys goods or pays for a service.
cards.example: The trader helped a customer choose a school bag.
cards.trap: Writing costumer for a buyer.

rule.text: Keep the word custom before er.

cards.meaning: Choose what to do or settle a question.
cards.example: The class will decide where to hold the party.
cards.trap: Writing the first vowel as i.

rule.text: Start with de followed by cide.

cards.meaning: With certainty or without doubt.
cards.example: Ada will definitely arrive before assembly.
cards.trap: Putting an a in the middle.

rule.text: Keep definite when adding ly.

cards.meaning: Unlike something else or distinct from it.
cards.example: The Aba market has different stalls for shoes and fabrics.
cards.trap: Dropping a letter from the double f.

rule.text: Write two f's before erent.

cards.meaning: Unhappy because things did not go as hoped.
cards.example: The Kano team was disappointed by the result.
cards.trap: Doubling the s in place of the p.

rule.text: Join dis and appointed, with one s and two p's.

cards.meaning: Likely to make someone feel awkward or ashamed.
cards.example: It was embarrassing to call the teacher by the wrong name at assembly.
cards.trap: Dropping one s or one r.

rule.text: Keep both r's and both s's from embarrass before adding ing.

cards.meaning: More than usual or more than others in the group.
cards.example: The market is busy, especially on Fridays.
cards.trap: Writing ex at the start.

rule.text: Write e before special and add ly.

cards.meaning: Of very high quality.
cards.example: Amina did an excellent job at the Enugu science fair.
cards.trap: Dropping an l.

rule.text: Keep the c after ex and write two l's.

cards.meaning: Activity done for health or for practice.
cards.example: The teacher gave us an exercise on fractions.
cards.trap: Writing an extra c near the beginning.

rule.text: Begin with exe and end with rcise.

cards.meaning: Towards the front.
cards.example: The driver asked the passengers to move forward in the danfo.
cards.trap: Dropping the r before w.

rule.text: Write for plus ward.

cards.meaning: Someone you know well and like.
cards.example: Chidi met his friend at the school gate.
cards.trap: Writing ei in the middle.

rule.text: Put i before e in friend.

cards.meaning: Thankful for help or kindness.
cards.example: The club was grateful for the books donated to the library.
cards.trap: Writing great at the start.

rule.text: Write grate before ful, with one final l.

cards.meaning: At the present time, often compared with the past.
cards.example: Nowadays, our school sends notices by text.
cards.trap: Dropping the a after now.

rule.text: Put an a between now and days.

cards.meaning: Having achieved what was planned.
cards.example: The fundraiser for the clinic was successful.
cards.trap: Doubling the final l or dropping a middle consonant.

rule.text: Keep both c's and both s's in success, then add ful.

cards.meaning: Introduces two possibilities or an indirect yes/no question.
cards.example: The pupils asked whether assembly would be indoors.
cards.trap: Dropping the h when writing the conjunction.

rule.text: Start with wh, with the second h in the th pair.
